land.text: Almería and its lands; the taifa 'originated in 1012' and 'declared independence from the Caliphate of Córdoba around 1012'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's first Almería shape is 1015; the Taifa overview page has Almería 1011-1091.

land.text: Almería and its district, 'captured on 17 October 1147' by Alfonso VII with Catalans, Genoese and Pisans; a third of the city to Genoa

successors.note: Almería passed to the Almohads in 1157 ('Six years later, Almería entered into Almohad possession'); the Castile and Almohad dossiers carry that. The first end, 1091, went to the Almoravids (ledger).

rulers.name: Ibn Aflah
rulers.note: List: '1012: Ibn Aflah (end year silent)'; the next entry is 1014.

rulers.name: Khayran al-'Amiri
rulers.note: A former Slavic slave from the Córdoba caliph's palace; the list gives 1014 and the next entry is 1028.

rulers.name: Zuhayr al-'Amiri
rulers.note: Former Slavic slave from Córdoba; a revolt among his troops led to his death 'in 1038'.

rulers.name: Abd al-Aziz al-Mansur
rulers.title: occupier from Valencia
rulers.note: King of Valencia: 'From 1038 to 1041 Almería belonged to the Taifa of Valencia'.

rulers.name: Abu Yahya Muhammad ibn Ma'n
rulers.note: List entry 1051; the next entry is 1091, and the end year 1090 is read from it. A regency of Abu 'Utba is listed 1052-1054 or 1055.

correction.text: Almería and its lands, Murcia independent until 1014 (Murcia page: independence 1011-1014)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1012-1013: the core of Almería before it took Murcia. The page says the taifa 'originated in 1012' (the list starts with Ibn Aflah in 1012); Cliopatria's first row is 1015. The infobox gives no area ('Area: Silent'), so the 14,798 km2 core could not be compared.

correction.text: Almería and the Murcian lands, held by Almería 1014-1038 (Murcia page infobox)

keyframe_review.note: 14,798 km2 (58 cells) draws only the Almería core, while Murcia has its own row 1015-1033. The Murcia page's infobox has 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065'; the shape is therefore the core plus the Murcian lands (Cliopatria's 23-cell Murcia shape) for 1014-1033.

20,948 km2: the core plus the 23 Murcian cells, a shape Cliopatria draws from 1034 although the Murcia page puts Murcia under Almería from 1014. Drawn 1034-1037 only: after Zuhayr's death 'in 1038' the Taifa of Valencia occupied Almería ('From 1038 to 1041 Almería belonged to the Taifa of Valencia').

correction.text: Almería and its lands, independent under Ma'n ben Muhammad ben Sumadih; Murcia remains with Valencia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1041-1045: Cliopatria has no Almería shape in these six years (it gives the land to Valencia, 1040-1045). The page: the Valencian governor Ma'n 'declared Almería independent again' (list entry 1041; infobox 'To Valencia: 1038-1042'); Murcia stayed Valencian until 1065 (Murcia page). Draw the core without Murcia.
14,798 km2 for 1046-1084: the core after Ma'n (1041) and Abu Yahya ibn Ma'n (list 1051), the regency of Abu 'Utba 1052-1054/55. The page dates no gain or loss in these years.

10,927 km2: the core less its north-eastern 16 cells. The page says 'Campaigns by the Taifa of Seville reduced its northern territory' without dates, so the loss in 1085 is Cliopatria's. Drawn 1085-1091 only: 'The kingdom finally was annexed to the Almoravid empire' (infobox 'To the Almoravid dynasty: 1091-1140'; Ahmad ben Muhammad ruled 'June to October or November 1091 only').

correction.text: Almería and its district as a second taifa, 1145-1147

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1145-1146: the second taifa, 'Almeria: 1145-1147 (briefly to Castile and then to Almohads)'; the Almería page's infobox has 'To the Almoravid dynasty: 1091-1140' and no 1145 entry. The 1147 shape is reused (the city and a smaller district).

8,968 km2 (35 cells): the second taifa's district. Drawn only until 17 October 1147 ('Almería was captured on 17 October 1147'); then Castile-held, with a third of the city to Genoa (Alfonso VII page), and Almohad from 1157. Cliopatria draws it to 1151.

correction.text: the city of Almería, in Ibn Hud's realm until his assassination there in 1238 and in the Emirate of Granada from then on; no separate taifa

keyframe_review.note: 5,153 km2 at 37.3-38.0 N (20 cells, 3 of them in Almería province; the city at 36.8 N is outside it): not a taifa the pages know. The Taifa overview page's third-taifa list (1228-1244) has no Almería entry; Almería was part of Ibn Hud's Murcian realm (he was 'assassinated in Almería in 1238') and 'belonged from then on to the Emirate of Granada' (Almería page). The cells are Jaén and Granada upland, held by Granada and Murcia, not by this state.

correction.text: the city of Almería, in the Emirate of Granada from 1238; no separate taifa

keyframe_review.note: 1,678 km2 (6 cells), 1241-1249: the same objection as 1236; none of the cells lie in Granada province. Almería 'belonged from then on to the Emirate of Granada' from 1238.

ledger.note: 1012: Almería declares independence from the Caliphate of Córdoba. 'The taifa originated in 1012'; it 'declared independence from the Caliphate of Córdoba around 1012', first ruler Ibn Aflah; the Taifa overview page has 1011. The page names the city and its lands only.

region.text: the Murcian lands, held by Almería 1014-1038

ledger.note: 1014: Khayran takes Murcia. The Murcia page's infobox: 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065' after independence 'from 1011 to 1014'; the Almería page lists Khayran from 1014 and does not mention Murcia (the Taifa overview lists Murcia 1011/1012-1065 as going to Valencia).

1038: Valencia occupies Almería. Zuhayr was killed by a revolt of his own troops 'in 1038' and 'From 1038 to 1041 Almería belonged to the Taifa of Valencia' under the emir Abd al-Aziz (infobox 'To Valencia: 1038-1042').
1038: the Murcian lands pass to Valencia. Infobox of the Murcia page: 'To Almeria/Valencia: 1014-1038 / 1038-1065'.

1041: Ma'n makes Almería independent again. 'The Valencian governor Ma'n later declared Almería independent again' (list entry 1041; the page's infobox says 1038-1042). The Murcian lands stay with Valencia to 1065.

region.text: the northern territory reduced by Seville's campaigns

ledger.note: 1085: the north-east of the taifa is lost. The page says only that 'Campaigns by the Taifa of Seville reduced its northern territory' and gives no dates; the Murcia page has Murcia under Seville 1078-1091. Cliopatria's shape narrows in 1085. Bridging judgment.

1091: the Almoravids annex Almería. 'The kingdom finally was annexed to the Almoravid empire, as were all of the other taifas' (infobox 'To the Almoravid dynasty: 1091-1140'); the Almería page's last ruler Ahmad ben Muhammad held it 'June to October or November 1091 only'; the Almería page: 'until 1091, when it fell to Almoravid control'. The Almoravid dossier dates the capture 'late 1091'.

1145: Almería is a taifa again. The Taifa page's second-taifa list: 'Almeria: 1145-1147 (briefly to Castile and then to Almohads)'; the Almería page's infobox gives the Almoravid period as 1091-1140, which leaves 1140-1145 unexplained.

17 October 1147: Alfonso VII takes Almería. 'Almería was captured on 17 October 1147' by a 'mixed army of Catalans and Franks, with a Genoese-Pisan navy' (Alfonso VII page, with García Ramírez of Navarre and Ramon Berenguer IV joining him); 'A third of the city was granted to Genoa'. The infobox: 'Annexed by Castile: 1147'.

wars.name: Valencian occupation of Almería
wars.outcome: After Zuhayr's death in 1038 Abd al-Aziz of Valencia occupied Almería; Ma'n declared it independent in 1041.

wars.name: Almoravid annexation of Almería
wars.outcome: The last Almería ruler Ahmad ben Muhammad ruled June to October or November 1091 and the kingdom was annexed to the Almoravid empire.

wars.name: Conquest of Almería
wars.outcome: Alfonso VII's mixed army with the Genoese-Pisan fleet captured Almería on 17 October 1147; a third of the city went to Genoa; Almería passed to the Almohads in 1157.
wars.note: Alfonso VII page: army of Catalans and Franks, García Ramírez of Navarre and Ramon Berenguer IV 'named as joining him'; Ibn Mardanish's role is not on the page.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened; the Seville frontier of the 1070s-1080s and the Murcian frontier are approximate. The Treaty of Tudilén (1151), which fixed Castile's and Barcelona's zones in Andalusia, falls after the state.

notes:
IDENTITY. The Taifa page gives 1012 (Cliopatria 1015; the Taifa overview 1011). The dossier runs 1012-1147 with two gaps: Valencian 1038-1041 and Almoravid 1091-1145. The Almería taifa in its second form (1145-1147) rests only on the Taifa overview page's list; the Almería page's own infobox ends the Almoravid period in 1140 and says 'Annexed by Castile: 1147'.
CLIOPATRIA. Shape 1015 (core only) and shape 1034 (core + 23 Murcian cells) disagree with the Murcia page, which gives Murcia to Almería from 1014; the dossier uses the core plus Murcia from 1014 (the Murcia dossier of this group corrects its 1015 shape in the same way). The 1040-1045 gap is Valencian in Cliopatria and per the Almería page only to 1041; a new keyframe covers 1041-1045. Shapes 1236-1240 and 1241-1249 are marked wrong: they lie in the Jaén and Granada uplands, not at Almería, and no page opened lists an Almería taifa after 1147. The infobox gives no area ('Area: Silent'), so no area comparison was possible.
UNSETTLED. (1) Zuhayr's occupation of Córdoba 'in 1035' (Almería page: allied with Granada against Seville) is undated at both ends and not drawn by Cliopatria; no event is written. (2) The date and land of the Seville campaigns that reduced Almería (ledger 1085, confidence 1). (3) 1140 versus 1145 for the end of the Almoravid period. (4) The Taifa overview lists Murcia 1011/1012-1065 as going to Valencia without an Almería interlude. (5) Almería in the Almohad period 1157-1228 and in Ibn Hud's realm 1228-1238 belongs to the Almohad and Murcia dossiers; the Emirate of Granada has the 1238 gain. (6) The Almoravid dossier dates the fall 'late 1091'; the Almería page gives the last ruler's months only.
PAGES. Five: Taifa of Almería, Taifa of Murcia, Almería (city), Alfonso VII of León and Castile, Taifa (overview). 'Conquest of Almería' and 'Conquest of Almería (1147)' do not exist as titles (url_not_found).
GAZETTEER. 'Almería' (admin1 and place) resolves.
